call: verb
telephone someone
typical: call + person, call a doctor/taxi/the police. NOT for: naming things.
I'll call you tonight.
We should call a doctor.
verb
have or give a name or title
typical: be called + name, call + person/thing + name. NOT for: phoning.
Our dog is called Max.
They decided to call the baby Emma.
verb
use a word or name to describe someone or something
typical: call sb a liar/fool, call it + noun. NOT for: official names.
Are you calling me a liar?
You can call it luck, but I call it hard work.
verb
ask or order someone to come to you
typical: call sb over/in/up. NOT for: phoning.
She called the waiter over.
He was called into the manager's office.
verb
arrange or announce an event
typical: call a meeting/strike/election. NOT for: phoning.
The union called a strike for Monday.
The minister called an election.
verb
say or shout something loudly
typical: call out, call for help. NOT for: phoning.
Someone called my name from across the street.
She called for help.
come: verb
move towards the speaker or the place being discussed
typical: come here/to + place/with me. NOT for: moving away (see go).
Come here, please.
Can you come to my party?
verb
go somewhere with someone
typical: come with us/along, come to dinner. NOT for: moving alone to the speaker.
Would you like to come with us?
He came along to the meeting.
verb
travel to or from a place, or have as origin
typical: come from + place, come by car/train. NOT for: leaving a place.
She comes from Poland.
We came by train.
verb
arrive, or happen at a certain time
typical: the bus/letter/summer comes. NOT for: people travelling.
A letter came this morning.
Christmas comes early this year.
verb
reach a position or level
typical: come first/second/last, come to an end. NOT for: moving to a place.
She came first in the race.
The meeting came to an end.
verb
be available or be sold in a certain form
typical: come in sizes/colours, come with + noun. NOT for: movement.
The shoes come in three sizes.
The phone comes with a charger.
verb
gradually begin to feel or know something
typical: come to realize/understand/like. NOT for: sudden events.
I've come to like this town.
He came to realize his mistake.
verb
become, usually by accident
typical: come loose/open/undone. NOT for: planned changes.
The knot came undone.
The door came open.
change: verb
become different
typical: thing + change, change from X into Y. NOT for: replacing something.
The weather changed quickly.
Her life has changed a lot.
verb
make someone or something different
typical: change + noun: plans, your mind, the law. NOT for: money.
She changed her plans.
He changed his mind about the job.
verb
stop using or doing one thing and start another, or replace something
typical: change jobs/schools/a tyre/the sheets. NOT for: gradual development.
He changed jobs in May.
I need to change the batteries.
verb
put on different clothes
typical: change + clothes/shirt, get changed. NOT for: replacing objects.
I need to change my shirt.
She got changed after work.
verb
move from one train, bus or plane to another
typical: change trains/buses/planes, change at + place. NOT for: clothes.
We changed trains in Prague.
You have to change at the next station.
noun
a difference or the process of becoming different
typical: a change in/of + noun, make a change. NOT for: money.
There has been a big change in the weather.
We need a change of plan.
noun
coins or money returned after paying
typical: keep the change, small change. NOT for: differences.
Keep the change.
Do you have change for ten euros?
